claims.statement: URE reports more than 1.6 million renewable microinstallations in Poland at the end of 2025, establishing a large fragmented installed-asset base.
The EU Data Act provides connected-product users access to readily available product data and a mechanism to direct sharing to a third party, subject to safeguards.

contrary_evidence: The Data Act permits restrictions where sharing would seriously undermine safety or security and protects trade secrets; it does not guarantee that every legacy inverter exposes useful data.

economics.acquisition_route: Begin through the founder's family renewable-installation channel, then white-label onboarding through regional installers using email, portal, and maintenance visits rather than founder-led events
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Reach 500 sites by year 2 (unvalidated), 5000 sites and PLN 9 million annual recurring revenue by year 5 (unvalidated), and a founder-owned equity value above PLN 5 million by year 6 (unvalidated)
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours per week during validation (unvalidated), with field capture delegated to installers
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software-led monitoring after field capture and installer revenue share; 65-78% gross margin (unvalidated)
economics.payback: Customer-acquisition and onboarding payback in 5-9 months (unvalidated)
economics.pricing: PLN 450-900 per monitored site per month (unvalidated), plus PLN 15000-50000 per governed benchmark engagement (unvalidated)
economics.retention_or_repeat: Thirty-six-month monitoring agreements (unvalidated) and repeated annual evidence reports (unvalidated)

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Every monitored operating month and resolved fault improves cross-brand failure baselines that a new entrant cannot recreate quickly
fingerprint.customer: Polish commercial PV owners, regional installers, renewable-asset insurers, and lenders
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installer-embedded onboarding during maintenance and commissioning
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Independent fleet monitoring plus controlled-access reliability benchmarks under data-contribution contracts
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Asset owner pays on monitoring activation; institutional buyer pays when receiving an approved aggregated reliability study
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A performance dispute, warranty claim, refinancing review, or unexplained yield loss

founder_fit: Uses data science and anomaly detection.
Leverages the family renewable-energy installation channel.
Allows asynchronous installer-led acquisition and part-time operation.
risks: OEM APIs may be incomplete or unstable.
Benchmark licensing demand and willingness to pay are unvalidated.
The stated PLN 90000 startup capital requirement is unvalidated.

structure.commercial_archetype: Permissioned asset-data cooperative with monitoring subscriptions and governed benchmark licensing
structure.control_point: Multi-year owner agreements granting telemetry access and an exclusive license to commercialize anonymized derived reliability features
structure.critical_dependency: Installers and asset owners must authorize technically usable data feeds without breaching OEM trade-secret, security, warranty, or personal-data restrictions

thesis: Contract with Polish photovoltaic owners and installers for permissioned access to inverter telemetry, maintenance outcomes, and scheduled thermal imagery; sell owners independent performance monitoring while licensing only aggregated, contract-authorized reliability benchmarks to insurers, financiers, and equipment suppliers. The defensible asset is a cross-brand longitudinal evidence corpus, not a dashboard wrapper.
title: Solar Fleet Evidence Cooperative
uncertainties: What share of target inverters exports sufficiently granular telemetry?
Will owners accept a durable derived-data license in exchange for monitoring value?
